t: Goal formalization from a broad question (foundational)
title: Goal formalization from a broad question (foundational)
description: A broad question is rewritten as an explicit goal statement naming the decision it will inform and the form the answer must take. Formalization forces the vague 'look into X' to become 'determine whether X meets criterion Y by date Z'. A goal that cannot be formalized this way is sent back for clarification instead of launching a doomed investigation. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
demo:
q = 'look into faster search'
goal = {'question': q, 'decision': 'choose index strategy', 'answer_form': 'latency comparison table', 'deadline': '2026-10-28'}
print('formalized goal:', goal['decision'], '->', goal['answer_form'])
print('measurable:', bool(goal['deadline'] and goal['answer_form']))
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Research Mission Planner practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Scope bounding with in/out lists (foundational)
description: The planner writes explicit in-scope and out-of-scope lists before any searching starts. Scope bounds prevent the classic failure where an investigation sprawls across adjacent topics and never finishes. Anything discovered outside scope is parked in a side list for future missions rather than pursued immediately. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.

title: Milestone planning with exit checks (foundational)
description: The investigation is divided into milestones, each with an exit check: a concrete, testable condition for moving on. Milestones are ordered by information value, so the most decisive evidence is sought first. If an exit check fails twice, the milestone is replanned rather than retried blindly a third time. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Research Mission Planner practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Resource budgeting per milestone (foundational)
description: Each milestone gets a budget of search steps, compute time, and source accesses. Budgets are set from the milestone's information value: decisive early milestones get more. When a milestone exhausts its budget without passing its exit check, the planner escalates instead of silently overspending. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.

title: Success criteria and stop rules (foundational)
description: The mission ends when its success criteria are met: the goal's answer form is filled with evidence-backed content, or a stop rule fires such as budget exhaustion or conclusive negative results. Written stop rules prevent zombie investigations that consume resources long after they stopped being useful. The final report states which criterion ended the mission. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
